paragraphs.title: The Approaching Enemy and the City’s Fear

easy.explanation: The passage says the enemy comes from the desert, from a terrible land.
easy.q: From where does the enemy come?

easy.explanation: His loins are filled with pain, and he is dismayed and fearful.
easy.q: What does the prophet experience when he hears the vision?

easy.explanation: The princes are commanded to arise and anoint the shield.
easy.q: What are the princes told to do?

medium.explanation: The passage mentions the treacherous dealer, the spoiler, and invading forces from Elam and Media.
medium.q: What combination of dangers appears in the passage?

medium.explanation: The phrase compares the prophet’s distress to the pains of a woman in labor.
medium.q: What does “pangs have taken hold upon me” describe?

answers: It makes the feast more joyful
It turns the night of pleasure into fear and leads to preparation
It causes the princes to ignore the danger
medium.explanation: The night of pleasure becomes fearful, and the princes are told to prepare the shield.
medium.q: How does fear affect the feast?

answers: Immediate danger requires a quick change from pleasure to defense
The city has defeated its enemies
challenge.explanation: The command to prepare the shield shows that the danger is urgent.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the movement from the table to the shield?

answers: It presents a peaceful and safe setting
It emphasizes the power and terror of the approaching threat
challenge.explanation: The desert whirlwind imagery creates a strong picture of an overwhelming enemy.
challenge.q: What is the effect of the desert-storm imagery at the beginning?

answers: The people move from preparation to celebration
The danger passes and peace begins
News of danger leads to fear and defensive preparation
challenge.explanation: The passage progresses from the frightening vision to fear and the command to prepare.
challenge.q: What development takes place in the passage?

paragraphs.title: The Watchman and the News of Babylon’s Fall

easy.explanation: The LORD tells the prophet to set a watchman who will declare what he sees.
easy.q: Whom does the LORD command to set?

easy.explanation: The messenger declares, “Babylon is fallen, is fallen.”
easy.q: What does the messenger announce at the end of the passage?

answers: They were moved to another city
They were broken to the ground
easy.explanation: The passage says the graven images of Babylon’s gods were broken unto the ground.
easy.q: What happened to Babylon’s graven images?

medium.explanation: The watchman is appointed to declare what he sees.
medium.q: What is the watchman required to do?

answers: A person who observes and reports
medium.explanation: The watchman stands on duty and reports the movements he observes.
medium.q: What is a watchman in this passage?

answers: A watchman is appointed, he keeps watch, and a messenger arrives
The messenger arrives before the watchman is appointed
The prophet hears the report without any watch being kept
medium.explanation: The passage first gives the command to set a watchman, then describes his vigilance and the arriving chariot.

answers: To show that reporting requires continual attention
To show that he left his post
challenge.explanation: He watches continually by day and through the nights, showing persistent attention.
challenge.q: Why is the watchman’s constant alertness emphasized?

answers: Both portray Babylon’s defeat and the overthrow of its gods
The images protect Babylon after its fall
The images are the messengers who bring the news
challenge.explanation: The city’s fall and the destruction of its images together show Babylon’s complete defeat.
challenge.q: What is the connection between Babylon’s fall and the breaking of the images?

answers: The prophet is reporting a message received from the LORD
The prophet is describing the strength of his army
The prophet is asking to build a tower
challenge.explanation: The prophet declares to his hearers what he has heard from the Lord of hosts.
challenge.q: What does “that which I have heard of the Lord” indicate?

easy.explanation: The burden of Dumah describes a call coming from Seir.

answers: What is the price of bread?
easy.explanation: They ask twice, “Watchman, what of the night?”
easy.q: What do they ask the watchman?

easy.explanation: He says, “If ye will enquire, enquire ye: return, come.”
easy.q: What does the watchman invite them to do?

answers: The morning and the night have come
The morning has not yet arrived
medium.explanation: The watchman says, “The morning cometh, and also the night.”
medium.q: What answer does the watchman give about the time?

answers: The place or people connected with the inquiry
medium.explanation: The passage begins, “The burden of Dumah,” identifying the subject of the message.
medium.q: What is Dumah in this passage?

answers: He gives a new and definite report
Time has passed, but he gives no new event
medium.explanation: He reports the passing of morning and night but gives no further news.
medium.q: What can be understood from the watchman’s answer?

challenge.explanation: The repeated question emphasizes expectation and the lack of a clear new report.
challenge.q: What feeling is created by the repeated words “watchman” and “night”?

answers: Because they may receive new information later
Because he wants to leave his post
challenge.explanation: His invitation leaves open the possibility of a later answer.
challenge.q: Why does the watchman invite the questioners to return?

answers: Time moves forward, but the report does not change
The city falls, but the images grow stronger
challenge.explanation: Morning and night pass, yet the watchman gives no new event or announcement.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in the watchman’s answer?

paragraphs.title: The Caravans’ Distress and the War Refugees

easy.explanation: The passage says, “In the forest in Arabia shall ye lodge.”
easy.q: Where must the caravans of Dedanim lodge?

easy.explanation: The inhabitants of Tema bring water to the thirsty and bread to the one who fled.
easy.q: What should the inhabitants of Tema bring to the thirsty traveler?

easy.explanation: They flee from swords, the drawn sword, the bent bow, and the grievousness of war.
easy.q: From what are the people fleeing?

answers: They are looking for a place to celebrate
They are fleeing the dangers of war
They are traveling to a feast
medium.explanation: The following verses explain that people are fleeing weapons and the grievousness of war.
medium.q: Why must the caravans lodge in the forest?

answers: A person moving away from danger
A person sitting on a throne
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to someone who has fled because of the war.

answers: They should provide water and bread
They should drive the refugees away
medium.explanation: Tema is described as bringing water and bread to those in need.
medium.q: What response is expected from the inhabitants of Tema?

answers: They are hiding or seeking shelter
They have reached their final destination
challenge.explanation: Lodging in the forest, together with the mention of fleeing, suggests danger and the need for shelter.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the caravans lodging in the forest?

answers: It presents the danger as real and widespread
It shows that there is no threat
It describes preparations for a feast
challenge.explanation: Swords and bows make the danger facing the refugees vivid and concrete.
challenge.q: How does the mention of weapons strengthen the picture of the situation?

answers: Refugees and travelers should be helped with food and water
Those who flee should be ignored
The refugees should be deprived of their goods
challenge.explanation: The passage highlights practical mercy through water and bread.
challenge.q: What human message comes from the command concerning Tema?

answers: At the end of that day
easy.explanation: The LORD says this will happen within a year, according to the years of an hireling.

answers: They will escape to the sea
easy.explanation: The passage says the residue of Kedar’s archers and mighty men shall be diminished.
easy.q: What will happen to the remaining archers and mighty men of Kedar?

easy.explanation: The passage concludes, “For the Lord God of Israel hath spoken it.”
easy.q: Who has spoken the words concerning Kedar?

medium.explanation: The loss of glory and the reduction of warriors together show Kedar’s downfall.
medium.q: What is the relationship between Kedar’s failing glory and the diminished archers?

answers: A definite, measured period of time
A period longer than ten years
medium.explanation: The comparison emphasizes a specific and measured time, namely one year.
medium.q: What does “according to the years of an hireling” emphasize?

answers: A change from great military strength to a diminished force
A change from a wandering people to a settled people
A change from war to guaranteed peace
medium.explanation: The remaining archers and mighty men will be reduced, showing the loss of military strength.
medium.q: What change is foretold for Kedar?

answers: The prophecy concerns a definite time, not merely a general threat
The event will occur that same night
challenge.explanation: The stated period gives the prophecy a specific and limited fulfillment time.
challenge.q: What does the exact time “within a year” emphasize?

answers: Kedar’s fighting strength will be affected
challenge.explanation: Archers and mighty men represent Kedar’s military power, which will be diminished.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from mentioning the archers and mighty men?

answers: By declaring that the LORD has spoken it
By announcing that Kedar has won
By inviting the people to question the watchman
challenge.explanation: The final statement grounds the prophecy in the word of the LORD God of Israel.
challenge.q: How does the passage conclude its description of Kedar’s fate?
